newsitem.title: INDIA: Chinese military commander leads team to India.
newsitem.headline: Chinese military commander leads team to India.

text.p: A senior Chinese military officer is visiting India to help strengthen ties between the two Asian giants, which fought a border war in 1962, officials said on Tuesday.
Lieutenant-General Liao Xilong, leading a seven-member delegation, met India's chief of army staff, General Shankar Roychowdhury, on Monday, the government said in a statement.
The Chinese visitors, who arrived on June 6 and were set to depart on Thursday, also met the vice chiefs of India's army, navy and air force.
Liao is commander of the Chengdu military region in southwestern China, the statement said. An army spokesman said it was the first time a Chinese regional commander had visited India.
"We are pursuing increased military-to-military contact for the sake of confidence-building," the spokesman said.
The government statement said it was significant that the Chinese commander was accompanied by foreign affairs officials.

"And as one of the frequent high and medium-level contacts in consonance with diplomatic parleys between the two countries, it is expected to enhance friendly relations and understanding between both," the statement said.
Chinese and Indian armies battled briefly on their Himalayan border in 1962 but tensions have eased in recent years with a series of high-level exchanges and agreements.
Beijing and New Delhi signed a pact in 1993 to ensure peace along their 4,000 km (2,500 mile) border and last year initialled a treaty to reduce troops and arms in the disputed regions.
India's vice chief of army staff, Lieutenant-General V.P. Malik, visited China in late May.

Liao was to visit defence and military establishments in different parts of India. Officials declined to reveal the sites but said they did not include the disputed region along the line of actual control dividing the two countries.
